headline: Check Point PHP2Shell and UnrealIRCd KEV deadlines fall today; FBI ARTEX AI tool warning and TSMC cloud-linked breach still lead

bullets.text: Due today, 11-16: the federal KEV deadline for Check Point CVE-2026-123039 (PHP2Shell, now the top developing story), where attackers gained root on gateways and deployed a VMware ESXi wiper, and for UnrealIRCd CVE-2026-114713 (server-level command injection).
Developing: the FBI warning that the ARTEX AI hacking tool is powering cyberattacks worldwide remains a 3-outlet story; the FBI flash alert of 11-13 describes attacks automated at machine speed.
Breaches: TSMC's employee data breach, tied to a cloud service provider, is a 3-outlet story; a hack at a French postal unit exposed data on 22 million people.
Still active: Cursor says a stolen Fireworks AI key led to the trojanized Claude Code extension incident; Uber separately reports driver licenses stolen via Fireworks AI.

SCKit: worm-like malware aimed at MSPs abuses ScreenConnect to deploy remote access and target technician sessions (Microsoft). Nothing new since the last sweep; the last 7 days score 0.99x the 90-day average, down from 1.23x.

actions: Check Point: if CVE-2026-123039 is not fixed yet, apply the vendor fix today, restrict management access, hunt for backdoors and keep ESXi backups offline.
UnrealIRCd: patch or take internet-facing servers offline today for CVE-2026-114713, and check them for injected commands.
Read the FBI ARTEX alert and confirm patching and alerting on internet-facing systems can keep pace with automated attacks.
Cursor and Claude Code users: review installed extensions against Cursor's disclosure and rotate any Fireworks AI API keys.
ScreenConnect: inventory instances and extensions, review technician sessions and hunt for SCKit using Microsoft's guidance.
Queue Cisco BroadWorks, Openwave, Outlook and Chromium fixes before the 11-24 KEV due date; SonicWall SSLVPN is due 11-20.
